extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: USPTO guidance for determining and applying §102(e) and §102(g) prior art dates when examining patent applications or reexamining patents, including special rules for U.S. and WIPO publications and patents derived from international (PCT) applications. Covers procedural steps, statutory interpretations, and illustrative examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactivity and effective date of amended §102(e) and §374
rubrics_metrics.description: The revised 35 U.S.C. § 102(e) (as amended by the AIPA and H.R. 2215) applies in the examination of all applications, whenever filed, and to the reexamination or contest of all patents, with only one exception related to potential references based on international applications filed prior to November 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: H.R. 2215’s revisions are completely retroactive to the effective date in the AIPA (November 29, 2000). The filing date of the application under examination is no longer relevant to deciding which version of §102(e) applies, except when the potential reference is based on an international application filed before November 29, 2000.

rubrics_metrics.name: What references qualify as §102(e) prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art under §102(e) includes U.S. patents, U.S. application publications (35 U.S.C. §122(b)), and certain WIPO publications of international applications (PCT Article 21(2)) where conditions are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (e) was split into §102(e)(1) for publications of patent applications and §102(e)(2) for patents; certain publications of patent applications (including some WIPO publications) can have prior art effect as of their effective U.S. filing dates when they meet the statutory conditions described in this notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for treating an international filing date as a U.S. filing date for §102(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international filing date (for an international application) is treated as a U.S. filing date for §102(e) prior art purposes only if: (1) the international application was filed on or after November 29, 2000; (2) it designated the United States; and (3) it was published by WIPO under PCT Article 21(2) in the English language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication under PCT Article 21(2) can result from early publication request or after the 18-month period. If these three conditions are met, the international filing date (or an earlier effective U.S. filing date properly claimed) can be the §102(e) prior art date for WIPO publications, U.S. application publications, and patents derived from the IA.

rubrics_metrics.name: International applications filed before November 29, 2000 are excluded from §102(e) bridging
rubrics_metrics.description: International filing dates prior to November 29, 2000 may not be relied upon as §102(e) prior art dates. Patents deriving from such international applications have §102(e) dates determined under pre-AIPA §102(e). WIPO or U.S. publications of international applications filed before that date have no §102(e) effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For patents that resulted from international applications filed before Nov 29, 2000, the §102(e) date is the earlier of the date of compliance with §371(c)(1),(2) and (4) or the filing date of the later-filed U.S. application that claimed the benefit. Publications of such IAs do not have §102(e) dates and may only be applied under §102(a) or (b) as of their publication dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional required conditions for IAs filed on/after Nov 29, 2000
rubrics_metrics.description: If an international application was filed on or after Nov 29, 2000, it must have designated the U.S. and been published in English under PCT Article 21(2) by WIPO for its international filing date to be a U.S. filing date for §102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to designate the U.S. or to have an English PCT Art.21(2) publication means the IA’s international filing date cannot be treated as a U.S. filing date for §102(e); such references may only be applied under §102(a) or (b) as of publication, or under §102(e) as of a later U.S. filing date that properly claims the IA if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an international application cannot serve as a bridge to an earlier filing
rubrics_metrics.description: International applications that (1) were filed prior to Nov 29, 2000, (2) did not designate the U.S., or (3) were not published in English under PCT Article 21(2) may not be used to reach back (bridge) to an earlier filing date through a priority or benefit claim for §102(e) prior art purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such IAs either have no §102(e) date or must be applied only under other statutory provisions (e.g., §102(a)/(b)) as of their publication date. Even if a later U.S. application claims the benefit of such an IA, the IA will not provide a §102(e) bridge unless it meets the statutory conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination step 1: determine effective filing date(s) of the application under examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Before applying prior art rules, determine the effective filing date(s) of the application being examined (including any proper priority/benefit claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP sections 706.02, 1893.03(b)/(c), 1895 and 1895.01 as revised by this notice for procedures on establishing effective filing dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination step 2: perform an appropriate prior art search
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should search for the most relevant prior art under §§102 and 103, including U.S. and WIPO publications of patent applications and U.S. patents accorded prior art dates under §102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search must consider the newly-created category of application publications (including qualifying WIPO publications) that may have earlier effective filing dates for prior art purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination step 3: determine whether the potential reference is 'by another'
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply a reference under §102(e), the inventive entity of the reference must be different from that of the application under examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where there are joint inventors, only one inventor need be different for the inventive entities to be different and a §102(e) rejection may be applicable even if there are some common inventors. See MPEP 706.02(a) for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination step 4: determine the appropriate §102(e) date for each potential reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the correct §102(e) prior art date for each potential reference by following specific subrules addressing the type and origin of the reference and any priority/benefit claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key subrules: (a) The potential reference must be a U.S. patent, a U.S. application publication (35 U.S.C. §122(b)), or a WIPO publication under PCT Art.21(2) to be applied under §102(e). (b) If the reference did not result from nor claim benefit of an IA, its §102(e) date is its earliest effective U.S. filing date, considering proper claims under §§119(e) or 120. (c) If the reference resulted from or claimed benefit of an IA, determine whether the IA satisfies: (i) filed on/after Nov 29, 2000; (ii) designated the U.S.; and (iii) published in English under PCT Art.21(2) — if so, the international filing date is a U.S. filing date and may be used as the §102(e) date (and can reach back to earlier filed U.S. or international applications if those earlier applications meet the same conditions). If the IA was filed on/after Nov 29, 2000 but did not designate the U.S. or was not published in English, do not treat the IA filing date as a U.S. filing date; apply the reference under §102(a)/(b) as of publication or under §102(e) as of a later U.S. filing date. If the IA was filed prior to Nov 29, 2000, apply pre-AIPA §102(e) rules: for patents use the earlier of completion of §371(c)(1),(2) and (4) or the filing date of the later-filed U.S. application claiming benefit; for U.S. application publications and WIPO publications of such IAs, never apply under §102(e) (only §102(a)/(b) as of publication). (d) Foreign filing dates claimed via §§119(a)-(d) or 365(a) (including international filing dates claimed as foreign priority) may not be used as §102(e) dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority/foreign filing dates are not §102(e) dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign applications’ filing dates claimed via 35 U.S.C. §§119(a)-(d) or 365(a) may not be used as §102(e) dates for prior art purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes international filing dates claimed as foreign priority dates under §365(a); the §102(e) date of a U.S. publication or patent remains determined by applicable U.S. filing/IA rules rather than foreign priority dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of §103(c) common-assignee (ownership) exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a §102(e) reference is used in an obviousness rejection under §103(a), ascertain whether the claimed invention and the reference were owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person at the time the invention was made, which may exclude the reference under §103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear statement of entitlement to the prior art exclusion by applicant(s) or a registered practitioner is sufficient evidence to establish the exclusion. However, a double patenting rejection based on the §102(e) reference could still be applied if appropriate. See MPEP 706.02(l) for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply references under the provision giving the best prior art date and procedural form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply references under §§102 or 103 based on which provision yields the best (earliest) prior art date for the disclosure. If a reference qualifies under multiple provisions (e.g., §§102(a) and (e)), apply under both as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should provide a copy of the appropriate statutory language under which the rejection is made in the first Office action utilizing such a rejection. Use only revised (October 2002, or more current) Form Paragraphs pertaining to §102(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection practice for new grounds based on §102(e) changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If a second or subsequent Office action contains a new ground of rejection necessitated by the change to §102(e) that was not also necessitated by claim amendment or certain information disclosure statements, that action cannot be made final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP 706.07(a) — examiners must avoid making final any second/subsequent action that introduces a new §102(e)-based ground not previously necessitated by claim changes or specified IDS items.

rubrics_metrics.name: §102(g) ex parte rejection requirements (conception, reduction to practice, diligence)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. §102(g) may form the basis for an ex parte rejection only if (1) the subject matter was actually reduced to practice by another before the applicant’s invention, and (2) there has been no abandonment, suppression, or concealment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conception alone is not sufficient; actual reduction to practice evidence is required. Filing an application is a constructive reduction to practice but generally does not provide evidence of actual reduction to practice during ex parte examination. Subject matter qualifying only under §102(g) may nevertheless be the basis for an ex parte rejection under §103. See cited cases (e.g., Amgen v. Chugai; Kimberly-Clark v. Johnson & Johnson; In re Zletz; In re Costello) and MPEP references for detailed precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness that WIPO publications may still have earlier §102(a)/(b) effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a publication of, or a U.S. patent issued from, an international application may not have a §102(e) date (or may have a §102(e) date after the effective filing date of the application being examined), the corresponding WIPO publication will likely have an earlier §102(a) or (b) date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should be aware of the possibility that a WIPO publication provides earlier prior art under §102(a)/(b) even when §102(e) bridging is unavailable; consider applying the reference under the statutory provision that gives the best prior art date.
